question.problem:
Consider the hexagon shown below. Draw an exterior angle of $\angle B.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14193271/assets/fc1834e88b4d08a2705059d28d21105047898f251f0f2c29f8509be7b6321de0.png)
question.worked_solution:
To construct an exterior angle of $\angle B,$ we extend $\overline{AB}$ past $B.$ The angle between $\overline{BC}$ and the extension of $\overline{AB}$ is an exterior angle of $\angle B.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14193271/assets/d91fc772042490e0785a4a617e4c3785c8616b7ed0ff05509ca8bc902eccc2a8.png)

Another way to construct an exterior angle of $\angle B$ is to extend $\overline{CB}$ past $B.$ The angle between $\overline{AB}$ and the extension of $\overline{CB}$ is also an exterior angle of $\angle B.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14193271/assets/8d031a6a6cc1513fc0a8031755b537d144279b88c964fc75728d3588ae1e4af9.png)
